## Introduction

In his celebrated work on the mod-$p$ properties of modular forms, Serre established a remarkable result concerning the $p$-adic behavior of Fourier coefficients of modular forms on the full modular group $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$. Specifically, for the primes $p = 2, 3, 5, 7$, Serre showed that the Fourier coefficients of an integral weight modular form on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with integer Fourier coefficients converge $p$-adically to a limit as one iterates a certain operator (typically involving powers of $p$ acting on the weight or through the Hecke operator $U_p$). This phenomenon reflects deep structural properties of the space of modular forms modulo small primes, and is intimately connected to the fact that these five primes are precisely those for which the corresponding modular curve $X_0(p)$ has genus zero, or more generally, for which the relevant spaces of modular forms exhibit particularly simple structure.

The present paper generalizes Serre's $p$-adic limit theorem beyond the classical setting of integral weight forms on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ to the broader context of weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight on the congruence subgroups $\Gamma_0(4N)$ for $N = 1, 2, 4$. Weakly holomorphic modular forms, which are permitted to have poles at the cusps, arise naturally in the theory of Borcherds products and in the study of mock modular forms, and their Fourier coefficients often encode arithmetic information of independent interest, such as class numbers, traces of singular moduli, and coefficients of Borcherds exponents. Extending Serre's result to this half-integral weight setting therefore opens the door to a range of new congruence phenomena.

The key technical ingredient in our proof is the establishment of explicit linear relations among the Fourier coefficients of modular forms of half-integral weight on $\Gamma_0(4N)$. These relations, which generalize classical recursions satisfied by coefficients of modular forms via the theory of modular equations and Hecke operators, allow us to control the $p$-adic behavior of the coefficients under repeated application of an appropriate $U_p$-type operator, and ultimately to establish the existence and identify the value of the $p$-adic limit for $p = 2, 3, 5, 7$.

As applications of our main theorem, we obtain several new congruence results in related areas of number theory. First, we derive congruences satisfied by the exponents appearing in Borcherds products, thereby extending known congruence properties of these exponents modulo small primes. Second, we establish congruences among quotients of Eisenstein series, which arise naturally in the study of half-integral weight forms and are closely related to generating functions for class numbers and related arithmetic quantities. Third, we deduce congruences for special values of certain $L$-functions at a specific point, connecting the $p$-adic limit theorem to central or near-central $L$-values via known formulas relating Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight forms to $L$-values (in the spirit of the Waldspurger and Shimura correspondences).

Finally, by invoking the Ikeda lifting—which associates to an elliptic modular form of appropriate weight a Siegel modular form of higher genus lying in the so-called Maass Space—we transport our congruence results for half-integral weight forms to the setting of Siegel modular forms. In particular, we obtain new congruences for the Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms in the Maass Space, thereby extending Serre's $p$-adic limit phenomenon to this higher-dimensional context as well. These results illustrate how the interplay between half-integral weight modular forms, Ikeda lifts, and classical $p$-adic techniques can yield a rich array of congruences across seemingly disparate areas of the theory of automorphic forms.

# Congruences for Fourier Coefficients of Half-Integral Weight Weakly Holomorphic Modular Forms and Applications

## 1. Introduction

In his foundational 1974 paper on the *p*-adic properties of modular forms, Jean-Pierre Serre established a remarkable result concerning the behavior of Fourier coefficients of modular forms on the full modular group $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. Specifically, for a modular form $f = \sum_{n \geq 0} a(n) q^n$ with integral Fourier coefficients, Serre showed that for $p \in \{2, 3, 5, 7\}$, the coefficients $a(n)$ satisfy a remarkable *p*-adic limiting behavior: as $n \to \infty$ along suitable arithmetic progressions, the coefficients converge $p$-adically to specific limiting values determined by the structure of the associated *p*-adic modular forms. This phenomenon is intimately connected to the fact that the Eisenstein series $E_{p-1}$ (or an appropriate substitute) is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$ for these small primes, a consequence of the classical Clausen–von Staudt theorem and related congruences for Bernoulli numbers.

Serre's original proof relied crucially on the theory of $p$-adic modular forms and the structure of the graded ring of modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, exploiting the fact that for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$ one has particularly simple descriptions of the space of modular forms modulo $p$. The restriction to these four primes is not merely technical but reflects a genuine arithmetic phenomenon: for larger primes, the relevant congruences fail to hold in the same uniform manner, and the *p*-adic limits, when they exist, exhibit fundamentally different behavior.

The present paper is devoted to extending Serre's theorem beyond the classical setting of integral weight modular forms on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ to the substantially richer context of **weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight** on the congruence subgroups $\Gamma_0(4N)$ for $N \in \{1, 2, 4\}$. Weakly holomorphic modular forms—modular forms that are permitted to have poles at the cusps—arise naturally in numerous contexts throughout number theory, including the theory of Borcherds products, the study of mock modular forms and harmonic Maass forms, and the construction of generating functions for arithmetic invariants such as class numbers and traces of singular moduli. The half-integral weight setting introduces substantial new technical difficulties, since the theory of half-integral weight modular forms lacks some of the structural simplicity of the integral weight theory (for instance, the absence of a straightforward multiplicative structure analogous to the ring of modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$), and the presence of poles at cusps requires careful control of the principal parts of the forms under consideration.

## 2. Main Result

Our main theorem establishes that Serre's *p*-adic limiting phenomenon, for the same set of primes $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$, persists in this broader setting: given a weakly holomorphic modular form of half-integral weight on $\Gamma_0(4N)$ (for $N = 1, 2, 4$) with algebraic (or, more precisely, appropriately normalized rational) Fourier coefficients, these coefficients satisfy an analogous $p$-adic convergence property along suitable arithmetic progressions of indices.

The proof departs significantly from Serre's original approach based on the theory of $p$-adic modular forms and the filtration of modular forms modulo $p$. Instead, our method is based on establishing and exploiting **explicit linear relations among the Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms**. These linear relations arise from the interplay between the spaces of holomorphic and weakly holomorphic forms in the relevant weight and level, together with the structure of the associated Kohnen plus-space, and they allow us to express the Fourier coefficients of a given weakly holomorphic form as explicit linear combinations of coefficients of a basis of forms whose $p$-adic behavior can be directly controlled. This approach has the advantage of being comparatively elementary and computationally explicit, while still yielding the full strength of the *p*-adic limiting statement in the half-integral weight setting. A key technical ingredient is a careful analysis of the principal parts at the cusps and their compatibility with the congruences modulo $p$, which requires new input beyond what is available in the classical integral weight theory.

## 3. Applications

The extension of Serre's theorem to weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight has a number of significant consequences, several of which we describe in detail.

**Congruences of Borcherds exponents.** Weakly holomorphic modular forms of half-integral weight serve as the input data for the Borcherds lifting construction, in which the principal part coefficients of such a form determine the exponents in an infinite product expansion of an automorphic form on an orthogonal group. Applying our extended theorem to these input forms, we obtain $p$-adic congruences among the exponents appearing in Borcherds products, for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$, generalizing known congruences for coefficients of classical modular forms to this more general product setting.

**Congruences of quotients of Eisenstein series.** Quotients of Eisenstein series of half-integral weight naturally furnish examples of weakly holomorphic modular forms with poles at the cusps, and their Fourier coefficients encode a variety of arithmetic information, including generating functions related to class numbers. Our result yields explicit $p$-adic congruences for the coefficients of such quotients, extending known results in the integral weight setting to this half-integral weight context.

**Congruences of special values of L-functions.** Via the Shimura correspondence and the Waldspurger-type formulas relating Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight forms to central or near-central values of $L$-functions of the corresponding integral weight newforms, our congruences for Fourier coefficients translate into $p$-adic congruences among special values of $L$-functions at a certain point (typically the central point of the functional equation), for the primes $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$. This provides new instances of the general philosophy that special $L$-values, suitably normalized, exhibit rich $p$-adic congruence structures.

**Congruences of Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms via the Ikeda lift.** Perhaps the most striking application arises from combining our result with the Ikeda lifting construction, which produces Siegel modular forms of higher genus in the Maass Spezialschar from elliptic modular forms (or, in the setting relevant here, from half-integral weight forms via the Shimura correspondence composed with the Ikeda lift). Since the Fourier coefficients of Ikeda lifts are given by explicit formulas in terms of the Fourier coefficients of the half-integral weight form being lifted, our $p$-adic congruences for the latter propagate, under the Ikeda lifting map, to $p$-adic congruences among the Fourier coefficients of Siegel modular forms lying in the Maass Space. This yields new congruences for degree $2g$ Siegel modular forms for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$, providing a higher-dimensional analogue of Serre's original phenomenon in a genuinely new arithmetic setting.

## 4. Organization

The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we recall the necessary background on half-integral weight modular forms on $\Gamma_0(4N)$, the Kohnen plus-space, and weakly holomorphic modular forms. Section 3 develops the linear relations among Fourier coefficients that form the technical core of our method. Section 4 contains the proof of the main $p$-adic congruence theorem for $p \in \{2,3,5,7\}$. Sections 5 through 8 are devoted to the four applications described above: Borcherds exponents, quotients of Eisenstein series, special $L$-values, and Siegel modular forms via the Ikeda lift, respectively.

# On Serre, Fourier, and Borcherds: Threads in Modern Number Theory

The history of modern number theory is woven from the contributions of mathematicians whose ideas, though developed in different eras, often intersect in unexpected and beautiful ways. Three names—Serre, Fourier, and Borcherds—represent distinct but interconnected strands in this rich tapestry, particularly in the study of modular forms and their applications.

**Jean-Pierre Serre**, one of the most influential mathematicians of the twentieth century, made foundational contributions across algebraic geometry, topology, and number theory. His work on modular forms, Galois representations, and p-adic methods has shaped the direction of arithmetic geometry for decades. Serre's conjecture, later proven by Khare and Wintenberger, exemplifies his ability to see deep structural connections between seemingly disparate areas of mathematics. His clear, precise writing style and his role in synthesizing and disseminating ideas—often through his correspondence and seminars—made him a central figure connecting many mathematical communities.

**Joseph Fourier**, though working over a century earlier in a very different context, established one of the most enduring tools in mathematical analysis: the Fourier series and Fourier transform. Originally developed to solve problems in heat conduction, Fourier analysis became indispensable far beyond its original application. In number theory, Fourier coefficients of modular forms carry deep arithmetic information—encoding partition numbers, representation numbers, and other combinatorial data. The Fourier expansion of a modular form is often the first and most natural way to extract concrete numerical information from an otherwise abstract object.

**Richard Borcherds**, a mathematician whose work bridges string theory, Lie algebra theory, and number theory, is best known for his proof of the Monstrous Moonshine conjecture, for which he was awarded the Fields Medal in 1998. Borcherds' theory of automorphic forms on orthogonal groups, and his construction of what are now called Borcherds products, reveal profound connections between infinite-dimensional Lie algebras, modular forms, and their Fourier expansions. These products often have infinite product expansions whose logarithmic derivatives connect back to classical Fourier coefficients, creating a bridge between Serre's arithmetic perspective and Fourier's analytic tools.

Together, these three names illustrate how mathematical ideas evolve and combine over time: Fourier's analytic techniques provide the language, Serre's arithmetic insights provide the structure, and Borcherds' revolutionary constructions provide surprising and deep connections that continue to inspire research in automorphic forms, string theory, and beyond.

# Abstract

Serre's classical theorem establishes that $p$-adic limits of integer weight modular forms with rational integer Fourier coefficients are themselves modular forms of $p$-adic weight, providing a foundational link between the $p$-adic and complex analytic theories of modular forms. In this paper, we extend Serre's framework to the setting of half-integral weight modular forms on $\Gamma_0(4N)$ for $N = 1, 2, 4$, establishing analogous $p$-adic limit theorems in this more delicate setting.

We show that if $\{f_i\}$ is a sequence of half-integral weight modular forms on $\Gamma_0(4N)$ with $p$-adic integral Fourier coefficients, and if the weights $k_i$ converge $p$-adically to some limit $k$, then the sequence of Fourier expansions converges $p$-adically (coefficientwise) if and only if the forms $f_i$ themselves converge $p$-adically with respect to the sup norm on Fourier coefficients; moreover, the limit is again the $q$-expansion of a half-integral weight $p$-adic modular form. Our approach adapts the Shimura correspondence and the theta-operator $\theta = q \frac{d}{dq}$ together with the theory of Katz's generalized $p$-adic modular forms, carefully accounting for the additional level structure at $4$ and the subtleties introduced by the metaplectic cocycle inherent to half-integral weight forms.

As applications, we construct new families of $p$-adic Eisenstein series and $p$-adic theta series of half-integral weight, and we determine explicit congruences among the Fourier coefficients of classical half-integral weight cusp forms, generalizing known congruences for coefficients of the Cohen-Eisenstein series and giving new instances of Ramanujan-type congruences for coefficients related to class numbers and representation numbers of quadratic forms. We further discuss the compatibility of our $p$-adic limits with the Shimura lift, showing that the $p$-adic limit operation intertwines suitably with the correspondence to integral weight $p$-adic modular forms established by Serre and Katz, and we describe the image of our half-integral weight $p$-adic modular forms under this lift in terms of $p$-adic families of eigenforms.

# Congruences of Borcherds Exponents, Eisenstein Series Quotients, and L-Function Values via p-adic Limits of Half-Integral Weight Modular Forms

## Abstract

We investigate arithmetic congruences satisfied by the exponents appearing in Borcherds product expansions, establishing connections to special values of L-functions through a systematic p-adic analysis of half-integral weight modular forms. Given a weakly holomorphic modular form of half-integral weight whose Fourier coefficients generate the exponents in a Borcherds lift, we construct a family of p-adic modular forms obtained as limits of sequences of holomorphic projections and theta-operator iterates. By exploiting the interplay between the Shimura correspondence and the structure of Eisenstein series quotients, we derive explicit congruences modulo powers of a prime $p$ for the Borcherds exponents in terms of divisor sums and coefficients of associated cusp forms.

Central to our approach is the identification of a p-adic limiting process under which normalized Eisenstein series quotients converge to generating functions whose coefficients encode both the exponents of the Borcherds product and critical values of the completed L-function attached to the underlying newform. This convergence is established using Serre's theory of p-adic modular forms together with a refined Kummer congruence adapted to the half-integral weight setting via the Shimura lift. We show that the resulting p-adic limit interpolates classical values $L(f,\chi,k)$ at critical points, extending prior results connecting Borcherds products to the arithmetic of L-functions.

As applications, we obtain new congruences for the coefficients of the classical partition-generating Borcherds lift and related eta-quotient exponents, recovering and strengthening known results of Ono, Bruinier, and Jenkins in special cases. We further demonstrate that the p-adic limit construction yields a conceptual explanation for previously conjectural congruences on Borcherds exponents associated to modular curves of genus zero, and we discuss extensions of these methods to forms of higher level and to Hilbert modular Borcherds products. Numerical examples for small primes $p \in \{2,3,5,7,11\}$ illustrate the density and structure of the resulting congruence classes, and we conclude with a discussion of potential applications to the Bloch–Kato conjecture and to explicit formulas for central L-values in families of half-integral weight modular forms.

**Keywords:** Borcherds products, half-integral weight modular forms, p-adic modular forms, Shimura correspondence, Eisenstein series, L-function special values, theta operator, Kummer congruences

# Abstract

Let $f$ be a half-integral weight modular form whose Fourier coefficients encode arithmetic data of independent interest—class numbers, Borcherds product exponents, or central values of quadratic twists of an $L$-function. In this paper we study linear relations among the coefficients $c(n)$ of such forms, obtained by combining the Shimura correspondence with the theory of modular forms modulo a prime $p$. Our main tool is a systematic analysis of the action of Hecke operators $T_{p^2}$ on half-integral weight forms in the sense of Kohnen plus space theory, together with the associated Galois representations attached to their integral weight Shimura lifts.

We prove that for a broad class of weakly holomorphic and holomorphic half-integral weight forms, the coefficients $c(n)$ satisfy exact linear congruences
$$
\sum_{i} a_i \, c(n_i) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^{\lambda}}
$$
whenever the indices $n_i$ lie in a fixed square class modulo $p$, with the constants $a_i$ and the exponent $\lambda$ determined explicitly by local data at $p$: the shape of the mod $p$ Galois representation attached to the Shimura lift, the $p$-adic valuation of related $L$-values, and the structure of the plus-space projection. These relations generalize and unify several known families of congruences for class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields and for coefficients of the Borcherds lifts of weakly holomorphic forms.

As applications, we derive:

1. **Congruences for Borcherds product exponents**: We show that the exponents in the Borcherds lift of a weakly holomorphic form of half-integral weight satisfy predictable congruences modulo powers of $p$, refining previous results on the integrality and divisibility of these exponents and producing new families of modular units on orthogonal Shimura varieties with prescribed divisor congruences.

2. **Nonvanishing and divisibility of central $L$-values**: Using the Waldspurger/Kohnen–Zagier correspondence between $c(n)^2$ and central values $L(f, n, 1/2)$ of quadratic twists of a fixed newform $f$, we translate our linear relations into congruences among twisted central $L$-values, yielding new criteria for simultaneous nonvanishing modulo $p$ and explicit lower bounds on the number of fundamental discriminants $n$ up to $X$ for which $p \mid L(f,n,1/2)^{\mathrm{alg}}$.

3. **Applications to indivisibility of class numbers**: Specializing to weight $3/2$ Eisenstein and cuspidal cases, we recover and strengthen classical results of Ono–Skinner type on the indivisibility of class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields, with explicit density estimates.

The proofs rely on an interplay between the theory of $p$-adic modular forms, the structure of the plus space under $U_p$ and $T_{p^2}$, and a careful study of the reduction mod $p$ of Borcherds' regularized theta lifts. We conclude with several conjectures suggesting that our congruences reflect deeper structure in the Iwasawa theory of half-integral weight forms and their associated $p$-adic $L$-functions.

# On p-adic Congruences of Modular Form Coefficients: Extension from SL₂(ℤ) to Γ₀(4N) with Applications to the Maass Space

## Abstract

We establish a systematic framework for extending p-adic congruences of Fourier coefficients of classical modular forms from the full modular group SL₂(ℤ) to congruence subgroups Γ₀(4N), and apply these results to construct and analyze p-adic congruences among Siegel modular forms lying in the Maass Space via the Ikeda lift.

Let f = Σ a(n)qⁿ be a normalized Hecke eigenform of weight k on SL₂(ℤ), and suppose f admits a p-adic congruence to another eigenform f′ modulo a prime p (or a fixed power pʳ), in the sense of Fourier coefficients: a(n) ≡ a′(n) (mod pʳ) for all n coprime to some auxiliary level. We show that such a congruence, initially formulated on the full level, propagates to forms of level Γ₀(4N) under mild hypotheses on p (typically p ∤ 2N and p greater than the weight, ensuring the relevant Hecke operators remain integral and the associated Galois representations are well-behaved at p). The key technical tool is a careful analysis of the trace and degeneracy maps between spaces of modular forms of level 1 and level 4N, combined with control of the p-adic valuations of Fourier coefficients via the theory of p-adic modular forms (in the sense of Serre and Katz) and the associated Up, and Vp operators. We show that congruences surviving the degeneracy maps correspond to genuine congruences of Hecke eigensystems on Γ₀(4N), and we quantify the level-raising and level-lowering phenomena that can occur, tracking the precise p-adic order of the congruence.

As the principal application, we transport these results to the setting of Siegel modular forms of degree n via the Ikeda lift. For F a Siegel Ikeda lift of a level-1 elliptic (or half-integral weight Kohnen plus-space) eigenform f, we show that the p-adic congruences established for f on Γ₀(4N) induce corresponding p-adic congruences among the Fourier coefficients of the lifted forms F, which naturally reside in the Maass Space of degree n Siegel modular forms of level Γ₀(4N)(N). Using the explicit Ikeda lift construction—expressing the Siegel Fourier coefficients of F in terms of divisor sums and special values of L-functions attached to f twisted by Kohnen plus-space data at level 4N—we derive explicit congruences

  A(F, T) ≡ A(F′, T) (mod pʳ)

for all matrices T of half-integral, symmetric, positive-definite type appearing in the Fourier expansion, where F and F′ are Ikeda lifts of congruent eigenforms f and f′. We further discuss the compatibility of these congruences with the standard L-function and with the structure of the associated Galois representations attached to Siegel eigenforms in the Maass Space, and we indicate applications to the Bloch–Kato conjecture and to detecting non-trivial elements in Selmer groups via congruences of Siegel Eisenstein and cuspidal Ikeda lifts at level 4N.

**Keywords:** p-adic congruences, Fourier coefficients, Γ₀(4N), Ikeda lift, Maass Space, Siegel modular forms, Kohnen plus space, Galois representations, level-raising.
